classification.difficultyReason: Form a quadratic area model from a three-sided fencing constraint and use its intercepts to locate the maximum.

content.prompt: A farmer has 360 metres of fencing and needs to create a rectangular paddock. There is a river that forms a straight natural boundary on one side. What are the dimensions of the paddock if its area is as large as possible? What is this largest area?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 17I.2, diagram below the stem in the left column
spec.description: River above a rectangular paddock; two perpendicular fences and the lower fence form a U. The perpendicular side is labelled x and the lower side y. Decorative blue river and green ground fills are omitted.
spec.mathematics: The river supplies one boundary, so only two lengths x and one length y require fencing.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no optimal dimensions or area are supplied.

answer.short:
Dimensions: $90\text{ m}\times180\text{ m}$. Maximum area: $16\,200\text{ m}^2$.

The area is greatest halfway between the zeros of $A=2x(180-x)$.
answer.worked:
The fencing covers three sides. Let $x$ be the perpendicular length and $y$ the length parallel to the river, in metres.

$$\begin{align*}2x+y&=360\\y&=360-2x\end{align*}$$

For $0<x<180$, the area is

$$\begin{align*}A&=xy\\A&=x(360-2x)\\A&=2x(180-x).\end{align*}$$

This downward-opening quadratic has zeros at $x=0$ and $x=180$. Its maximum occurs halfway between them:

$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{0+180}{2}=90\\y&=360-2(90)=180\\A_{\max}&=90(180)=16\,200.\end{align*}$$

The paddock should be $90\text{ m}$ perpendicular to the river and $180\text{ m}$ parallel to it. The largest area is $16\,200\text{ m}^2$.
